To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-1 family members IL-1F4, IL-1 F5, and IL-10 activate the IL-1R pathway through the IL-1RI/IL-1RacP complex.
three novel members of the IL- 1 family signal through the IL-1R complex to activate the pathway leading from NF-κB.
the newly discovered cytokines IL-1F1-IL-1F10 activate the pathway leading through IL-1RA and IL-1RACp and that this pathway is activated by IL-1, IL-18, and the novel IL-1 family members.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the receptors for novel cytokines and the elucidation of the mechanisms of their signal transduction.
understanding how IL-1F cytokines are involved in the regulation of immune responses and inflammation, and how the IL-1R system has expanded to include new members.
understanding how IL-1F cytokines are produced by the cells and the mechanisms by which they signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the IL-1F cytokines are capable of activating NF-κB, MAPKs, and other signaling cascades, and that they do so through the IL-1R family member, IL-1R rp2, which is also required for signaling by IL-1 itself.

the three novel cytokines IL-1F1 to IL-1 F3 signal through a novel IL-1R, IL-1R8, and that this signaling is dependent upon the presence of IL-1RAcp, which has a similar function as the IL-1R1 in IL-1 signaling.
IL-1R2, IL-1R1, IL-1RAcp, and IL-IRrp2 are the receptors of IL-1 family members.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IL-1F cytokines activate the pathway leading through the IL-1 receptor complex to activate the NF-κB pathway and the MAPKs.
the IL-1F family members signal through IL-18R and IL-1RI, and IL-18F, IL-1β and IL-1α signal through IL- 1RI and IL-1RacP, whereas IL-1F4, IL-1RII, and IL-36α, β and γ signal through IL-36R.

all members of the IL- 1 family, including the newly discovered family members IL-1F1 to IL-1 F10, signal through the same receptor complex, which is composed of two chains, IL- 1Rrp2/IL-1RAcPII and IL-1RacPI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL-1R2 is a receptor for IL-1F family cytokines.
IL-1R2 and IL-RAcP are both required for signaling by the IL-1F family members.
the three novel IL-1 family members signal through IL-IRrp2 and IL-RacP in a manner similar to IL-1β.
